subject.title: feat(memory): carry source actor context into recall

question: Should OpenClaw accept SourceActor as the public plugin/message/memory attribution contract for this stack, or should the contract be renamed or narrowed before release?
rationale: The code is plausible, but this PR creates plugin-facing API and prompt/memory semantics that external integrations can depend on after release, so automation cannot choose the long-term naming, privacy boundary, or stack timing.

options.title: Approve SourceActor Contract
options.body: Treat this PR as the memory follow-up after the prerequisite Signal/source-actor stack lands and resolve draft status before merge.

options.title: Rename Or Narrow Contract
options.body: Ask for a revised API surface if maintainers want different names, fewer scalar mirrors, or stricter privacy boundaries before release.

options.title: Pause The Stack
options.body: Keep the PR draft or close later if maintainers decide participant attribution should be structurally stored before exposing best-effort context.

recommendation.title: Approve SourceActor Contract
recommendation.body: Treat this PR as the memory follow-up after the prerequisite Signal/source-actor stack lands and resolve draft status before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing history is on inbound context centralization, plugin descriptor context, plugin tool context, and memory runtime behavior near the public contract boundary.
